subject: Customer comms: tail latency stability work (KV cache fragmentation / compaction) — timing + positioning

body:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Customer comms: tail latency stability work (KV cache fragmentation / compaction) — timing + positioning

Mateo / Neha —

Following the Feb 11 incident + a couple of escalations (SUP-4391, SUP-4410), CS/Sales are asking what we can say to a few Dedicated accounts that are (a) sensitive to p99 during bursts and (b) asking “what’s actually changing + when”.

Can you help me with:
1) A realistic timeline we can share (canary vs broad rollout).
2) The safe positioning language (no breaking behavior, no customer action required, etc.).
3) Any hard “don’ts” (numbers we should avoid, scope boundaries).

Goal is a short blurb CSMs can paste into customer emails + a slightly longer paragraph for exec update calls.

Thanks,
Nikhil
—
Nikhil Sharma
Product — Hosted API
Redwood Inference



From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 10:01 AM PST
Subject: Re: Customer comms: tail latency stability work (KV cache fragmentation / compaction) — timing + positioning

Yep.

What’s changing (high level): runtime memory-management work around the GPU KV cache (fragmentation metrics + allocator improvements + online compaction/eviction that’s scheduler-aware). This is specifically targeted at bursty/mixed-length traffic where we currently see holes in the cache → extra allocator churn → tail spikes.

Timeline (tentative but directionally correct):
- Week of Mar 10: canary on one Hosted region + one Dedicated pool (flagged, default off).
- Late Mar: expand to more pools/regions if canary looks good (25% then broader).
- Early Apr: default-on consideration (still depends on canary + any pool/model-specific tuning).

How to describe:
- “Stability improvement” vs “performance upgrade.”
- No API changes, no model behavior changes.
- Rollout is gradual and monitored; we can roll back quickly if signals regress.

Don’ts:
- Don’t promise a specific p99 number across all workloads. The win is biggest on burst + mixed context distributions.
- Don’t imply it eliminates all tail latency; it reduces one driver we’ve identified.

If you want, I can send a 2–3 sentence version you can hand to CS.

Mateo



From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 8:34 AM PST
Subject: Re: Customer comms: tail latency stability work (KV cache fragmentation / compaction) — timing + positioning

+1 to Mateo’s framing.

A few comms guardrails from the canary-risk review side:

Language to use:
- “Feature-flagged runtime improvement” / “incremental rollout” / “continuously monitored.”
- “No breaking change” / “no customer migration required.”
- “Focus is reducing fragmentation-related allocation churn that can amplify tail latency during bursts.”

Language to avoid:
- Avoid “defragmentation” (sounds like offline maintenance / downtime). Prefer “online compaction” or “allocator improvements.”
- Avoid any claim that could be read as an SLO change/commit (e.g., “we will meet X ms p99”).

Timing language to use:
- “Starting in March” (canary) and “rolling out more broadly over subsequent weeks” is safer than naming an exact date for default-on.

If a customer asks “can we get this earlier?”
- We can say: “We can discuss early enablement for Dedicated once the canary gates pass; it’s controlled by a runtime flag.”

Neha
—
Neha Kapoor
Infrastructure & Reliability Leadership
Redwood Inference



From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 11:09 AM PST
Subject: Re: Customer comms: tail latency stability work (KV cache fragmentation / compaction) — timing + positioning

Thanks — drafted two variants below. Please mark up.

A) Short blurb for CSM email (Dedicated / Hosted):
“We’re rolling out a runtime stability improvement focused on reducing GPU KV-cache fragmentation effects that can contribute to p99 spikes during bursty traffic. This is an internal serving-runtime change (no API changes, no model behavior changes, no customer action required) and will be introduced gradually via canary in March with monitored rollout in subsequent weeks.”

B) Slightly longer paragraph for exec update calls:
“We identified KV-cache fragmentation under mixed sequence-length burst traffic as a contributor to tail latency variability in some pools. The runtime team is shipping allocator + ‘online compaction’ improvements and additional telemetry to reduce allocation churn and lower the probability of allocator-related tail spikes. The change is feature-flagged and will be rolled out gradually starting with a canary in March; we’ll monitor pool-level signals and can quickly roll back if we see any regressions. There are no API changes and no changes to model outputs.”

Questions:
1) Is “online compaction” OK or do we want even less technical?
2) Any additional sentence on “what we’ll be monitoring” that’s safe to include?

Nikhil

Edits inline below.

A) Short blurb
Good. Minor tweak: “KV-cache memory fragmentation” (so it’s clear it’s not semantic caching).

Suggested:
“We’re rolling out a serving-runtime stability improvement focused on reducing GPU KV-cache memory fragmentation effects that can contribute to p99 spikes during bursty traffic. This is an internal runtime change (no API changes, no model behavior changes, no customer action required) and will be introduced via canary in March with monitored rollout over the following weeks.”

B) Longer paragraph
Also good. I’d keep “online compaction” but in quotes once, then simplify.

Monitoring sentence (safe):
“We’ll be monitoring tail latency, allocation failure rates, and compaction/eviction overhead per pool/region as we expand rollout.”

I’d avoid mentioning exact region/pool names in customer-facing comms.

Mateo
